messages.subject: Help need for using viewports
parts:
I am trying to do something similar to chapter 8 of the ggplot2 book.
I can't for the life of me see why the following code creates separate
pages for each plot. I have tried the on screen device and the pdf
device and tried a smaller number of grids but nothing works.
Any help will be appreciated. The code fragment:


agPlotList <- lapply(comboAg15minFrameList,
function(comboFrame){
s <- comboFrame$Symbol[1];
p <- qplot(BarNo,weight=NoContracts/
1000,data=comboFrame,
geom='bar',

facets=studyYear~.,ylab='Volume(Thousands)',
xlab='Intra-day 15 minute period
(1-15)',
main=paste(s,' - Intra-day Volume
Distribution (by year)', sep=''));
p <- p+opts(plot.title=theme_text(size=12));
p <- p
+opts(panel.background=theme_rect(colour=NA));
p <- p+opts(axis.text.y=theme_text(size=6));
p;
});

#pdf(file="agTODVol.pdf",width=7,height=7);
grid.newpage();
pushViewport(viewport(layout=grid.layout(2,1)))
vplayout <- function(x,y) viewport(layout.pos.row=x,layout.pos.col=y);
#print(sample.plot,vp=vplayout(1,1:2));
print(agPlotList['C'],vp=vplayout(1,1));
print(agPlotList['O'],vp=vplayout(1,2));
print(agPlotList['S'],vp=vplayout(2,1));
print(agPlotList['W'],vp=vplayout(2,2));

dev.off();

MC

messages.author: 5a1b5a9591c118ef
messages.subject: Re: Help need for using viewports
parts:
Hi,

Consider this minimal example,

l = lapply(letters[1:3], function(l) qplot(1:10, rnorm(10), main=l))
names(l) = letters[1:3]

> is(l['a'])
[1] "list" "vector"
>
> is(l[['a']])
[1] "ggplot"

So my guess is that you are printing lists instead of ggplots,
therefore the viewport argument is ignored. Using [[ should solve your
problem:


source("http://gridextra.googlecode.com/svn/trunk/R/arrange.r")

arrange( l[['a']], l[['b']], l[['c']])

or

do.call(arrange, l)
will do the same thing more concisely.

HTH,

baptiste
